other.label: Outside
other.note: another workspace, a phone or a service

pages.title: A ticket's life
pages.one: Every piece of work is a ticket. It moves through a few states; you move it to Done (or the Reviewer, if you turned it on).

moves.text: Asks you, or waits for a time or another ticket
The wake time comes, or the other ticket reaches Check or Done
The helper stopped before it finished
The Reviewer accepts a small, safe change (only if you turned it on)

good: The helper doing the work can never move its ticket to Done. The furthest it gets is Check.
The board shows two more lanes: Needs you (a question is open) and Superseded (another ticket replaced it).

cmds: the helper says it is finished: Check
files: files, evidence and what was looked at

pages.title: After you make a ticket
pages.one: From your words to a helper at work.

steps.text: You write what you want
steps.detail: In New ticket, by phone, or with Make ticket in Chat.

steps.text: orch saves it in Backlog
steps.detail: Long text gets the first words as a stand-in title.

steps.text: Start it now?

branch.then: It stays in Backlog; nothing runs

branch.if: Start (a text from the phone starts by itself with Automation on)

steps.text: orch picks the model
steps.detail: Design, look, security, concepts or long text: the big model. Clearly small (a typo, one word): the smaller one. Unclear: the big one.

steps.text: orch checks if a helper can start now

branch.if: Your helper limit is reached or the computer is busy
branch.then: The ticket waits its turn and starts by itself

steps.text: The helper writes a clear title and description
steps.detail: Also what Done means and its estimate of time and cost. It never changes a title you wrote.

steps.text: It splits the work into tasks
steps.detail: One task per piece of your work, before it starts.

steps.text: The helper starts on the tasks

good: There is no separate sorting robot: the model pick is a fixed word rule in orch, and the tidy-up is the helper's first job.
Making a ticket only saves it; a helper starts when you press Start or Automation starts it.

cmds: the helper writes the real title
a bigger model, with a reason

pages.title: How a helper works
pages.one: Tasks, evidence for each task, and a question only when it really needs you.

steps.text: Reads what you wrote and any new message
Starts one task
Does it and adds evidence
steps.detail: Evidence is a pull request, a file, a link, a command it ran, or a note. A task without evidence cannot be ticked.

steps.text: Needs you?

branch.if: Cannot be undone, costs money, touches production, deletes real data, or others see it
branch.then: It asks you with options and a suggestion, and goes on with the rest

steps.text: Tasks left?

branch.if: No, and no open question or unread message

steps.text: Sends the ticket to Check

good: orch refuses evidence that contains a password or key, and refuses a question that asks you for one.
When a check it ran fails twice on the same task, the ticket moves up to the big model by itself.

cmds: one task per piece of work
a task is done only with evidence
a check the next run can repeat

pages.title: Questions and cards
pages.one: One way to ask: a question on the ticket. You answer wherever you are.

steps.text: Asks a question with options and a suggestion
steps.detail: Something to look at comes as a card: a choice with pictures, a draft, a plan, a before and after, a link.

steps.text: The ticket waits; the question shows under Needs you
steps.detail: On Home, on Review and on your phone.

steps.text: Keeps working on what does not depend on it
You answer on the computer or the phone
The helper goes on with your answer

good: Drafts, designs and choices with pictures are yours alone: no helper, script or reviewer can answer them for you.
Silence is not an answer, unless you turned on Reviewer answers: then a plain question gets the suggested option after 30 minutes (never a card, a draft, looks, words, money or production).

cmds: everything that waits for a person
files: when a helper must ask (if you wrote one)

pages.title: Check and Done
pages.one: The helper finishes, you check. An optional Reviewer can take small, safe ones off your desk.

steps.text: Sends the ticket to Check with a short summary
Is the Reviewer on?
The Reviewer accepts for you only when all is true
steps.detail: Every task has evidence, no open question, its pull request merged with green checks, a small change, and nothing about look, words, concepts, structure or security.

branch.then: It leaves it for you with one line why

steps.text: Accept: Done. Or ask for changes: back to the helper with your note

good: A ticket with a draft, mockup or design always waits for you.

cmds: the page with what waits for you

pages.title: Which model works on it
pages.one: The smaller model for small work, the big one for the rest. It only ever moves up.

steps.text: Before each start, orch reads the ticket

branch.if: Clearly small: a typo, one word, a label
Design, look, security, concepts, add-ons, long or unclear

steps.text: Moves up by itself when
steps.detail: A check fails twice on the same task, or the helper stopped twice with open tasks.

steps.text: Can ask to move up, with one line why
Your own pick always wins
steps.detail: The fastest model and the drafts model are only ever your choice.

good: On the drafts model a helper builds at least three different drafts, has each one challenged, and shows them side by side.

cmds: move up, never down by itself
tokens per model and per ticket

pages.title: How many helpers work at once
pages.one: A few helpers work at once. Other tickets wait their turn and start by themselves.

steps.text: A ticket should start
Fewer helpers than your limit, and the computer not too busy?

branch.then: It waits its turn: high, normal, low priority, then oldest first

steps.text: A helper finishes: its ticket goes to Check, or it sat idle too long
The next waiting ticket starts

good: A brake stops runaway work: at most 20 automatic starts per ticket per day, and Pause stops all new starts.

pages.title: Chat
pages.one: Talk first, make a ticket when it is clear.

steps.text: You write in Chat, on the computer or the phone
A helper answers and links tickets, files and pages
When it is clear: "Shall I make this a ticket?"
steps.detail: A card with the proposed title. The helper may never make the ticket itself.

steps.text: You press Make ticket
The talk since the last card becomes the ticket's note

good: Chat is one conversation per workspace; a new day starts at 04:00.

files: the conversation, one file per day

pages.title: What runs by itself
pages.one: orch looks after its helpers in short rounds. Programs do this, not AI.

steps.text: A helper idles with open tasks

branch.then: A fresh start, at most every 6 hours

steps.text: A ticket is finished or only waits

branch.then: The helper is closed so another can start

steps.text: A ticket waits for another ticket
The usage limit ran out
One manager helper per workspace is always there
steps.detail: It keeps its conversation across stops and never waits its turn.

good: The rounds come from the Automation add-on; without it, orch only does what you start.

pages.title: How add-ons plug in
pages.one: An add-on adds a page, buttons, ticket fields and helper know-how. orch itself never depends on one.

steps.text: You turn an add-on on in Settings
orch reads its description card
steps.detail: A small file that lists what it brings. orch never runs add-on code to find out.

steps.text: It shows up
steps.detail: A tab under Add-ons, rows on the ticket, buttons and a skill for helpers.

steps.text: Its own pages appear here
steps.detail: New with this page: the description card names the add-on's documentation pages.

steps.text: Helpers learn it from its skill
Turn it off: everything hides, ticket data stays

good: New with this page (to be built): every add-on brings its own documentation pages. An add-on that is off keeps its pages readable here, marked Off.

cmds: what its dashboard tab shows (add-ons with a tab)
files: in the add-on: its tab, commands and doc page

pages.title: Keys and passwords
pages.one: Keys stay in a private folder. Nothing leaves with a recognised key in it.

steps.text: Keys live in a private folder that git ignores
Uses a key by handing it straight to a command, never printing it
Checks every evidence, message and upload before it leaves

branch.then: Nothing is sent; it says which line, never the value

good: A helper may never ask you to type a password or key into a question.

cmds: look for keys in text (reads stdin)
logins and tools: works or not
files: private; never shared, synced or sent

pages.title: One copy per ticket
pages.one: Each code ticket gets its own working copy, so helpers never edit in each other's copy.

steps.text: A helper starts on a code ticket
It gets its own copy of the project
Works and saves changes on its own branch
The work joins the project later, through a pull request; the copy is removed when the ticket closes

files: where a ticket's changes are saved
